arguments.value: Erchonia gave InnerScope an exclusive, non-transferable right to market and sell specified Erchonia products worldwide, but only to approved licensed healthcare professionals and only for treating hearing disorders. InnerScope must use best efforts to promote the products, meet minimum performance goals, keep sales records, report complaints and sales information, follow Erchonia’s product-use rules, pay on time, and not sell competing products without permission. Erchonia can change or discontinue products, owns all intellectual property and trademarks, and controls how its marks are used. The agreement lasts three years and renews for three-year periods if both sides agree on new performance goals. Either side can terminate for material breach after notice and a cure period, and Erchonia can terminate immediately if InnerScope becomes insolvent or bankrupt. The contract includes confidentiality, warranty disclaimers, mutual indemnities, arbitration, Florida governing law, and other standard legal terms.
